name: Amazon RDS
tagline: AWS's managed service for six relational engines: PostgreSQL, MySQL, MariaDB, Oracle, SQL Server and Db2.
description: Amazon RDS is AWS's long-running managed service for standard relational engines: PostgreSQL, MySQL, MariaDB, Oracle, SQL Server and IBM Db2. AWS handles provisioning, patching, automated backups with point-in-time restore, Multi-AZ failover (including the two-readable-standby cluster option) and read replicas, while you keep the stock engine behavior and choose instance and storage types. RDS Custom allows OS-level access for Oracle and SQL Server, and RDS Proxy pools connections. It is the safe default when you want a familiar engine on AWS without Aurora's proprietary storage layer or pricing, though you get vertical scaling only and must plan major-version upgrades.

pricing.notes: Per instance-hour plus storage and I/O; Reserved Instances for discounts; Oracle/SQL Server/Db2 license-included or BYOL. AWS Free Tier covers small instances or credits for new accounts.

scale.notes: Vertical scaling up to 64 TiB storage per instance; up to 15 read replicas (engine-dependent), including cross-region.

strengths: Stock engines with predictable behavior and easy migration in or out
Six engines, including licensed Oracle, SQL Server and Db2
Automated backups, point-in-time restore and Multi-AZ failover
RDS Proxy for connection pooling from Lambda and microservices
weaknesses: Vertical scaling only; no built-in write sharding
Failover is slower than Aurora's shared-storage design
Storage and IOPS tuning (gp3/io2) adds operational decisions
AWS-only and no superuser access to the instance
useCases: Lift-and-shift of existing PostgreSQL, MySQL or Oracle apps to AWS
Standard web and line-of-business application backends
Licensed commercial databases without managing servers
Cost-sensitive workloads where Aurora is overkill
